suites.why: The tracker is this guard's whole subject, and the failure it exists for is a live outside-the-tree caveat with nothing saying how to re-check it. A fixture cannot show that the *real* rows are the ones being read: the guard resolves each caveat's key against `ledger/`, and a key that has drifted makes a row invisible to it while the file still parses.

cases.name: the npm caveat loses its recheck, the state every one of them was in

suites.why: The directory of draw records is this guard's whole subject, and a fixture cannot show that the real one is being read: the guard globs `ledger/draws/*.json` and joins the records to `docs/caveat-status.json` by key, so a path that has drifted makes every record invisible while every fixture case still passes. Breaking the one record in the tree is the only thing that proves the glob resolves.

cases.name: the recovered draw cites an entry that is not there

unmutated.check_build_output: Its subject is the absence of a thing: no build output is tracked, and every package root ignores its own. A mutation would have to *add* a tracked artifact, which `scripts/mutate.py` cannot express -- its patches replace text in one file, and this needs a new file plus a .gitignore edit. Its fixture tests cover the rules over a tree they build.
